label: Product mode: not part of the pre-registered experiment

templates.description: A panel on a revolute hinge: a lid opens upward about its back edge, a door swings about a side edge.
templates.note: A tote lid, a hatch, a cover or a cabinet door. orientation lid: a horizontal panel hinged along its back edge, its closed underside 120 mm above the table (there is no hinge-height parameter; 120 mm is a default bin's height, so a lid at a bin's position covers a bin of that height); it stays open only past vertical. orientation door: a vertical panel depth_mm wide and width_mm tall, 10 mm above the table, hinged on its left edge, opening toward its front. It starts closed; angle_deg is 0 closed, positive open.
templates.model: revolute joint with damping, a hinge stop and an optional opening torque (spring or detent)

params.name: depth_mm
params.description: Panel depth from the hinge to the free edge

params.name: open_torque_nm
params.description: Torque that resists opening at the hinge

params.name: feature
params.description: What a hook can engage at the free edge

templates.description: A box on a prismatic slide with friction, opened by a bar, lip or knob handle.
templates.note: A drawer in a cabinet or shelf unit. It starts closed; travel_mm is 0 closed, positive open.
templates.model: prismatic joint with friction loss and end stops

params.name: travel_mm
params.description: Slide travel to the open stop

templates.description: A slot or wing head on a revolute joint with a detent and a stop at the end of its turn.
templates.note: A panel fastener or cam lock on its own plate. It starts locked at its stop and opens counter-clockwise seen from above (twist ccw); angle_deg counts counter-clockwise from locked. Locking a latch that starts locked is not modelled.
templates.model: revolute joint with a torque to open, a detent and a stop
templates.caveat: Latches are an approximation: a detent torque on a revolute joint; no cam or spring geometry.

params.name: head
params.description: Head shape: a slot for a blade or a wing to grip

params.name: turn_deg
params.description: Turn from locked to open (the stop)

params.name: detent
params.description: A detent holds it locked until the torque is exceeded

templates.description: A cap, coupling or nut that starts on a fixed threaded seat and tightens to a final torque.
templates.note: A pipe coupling, cap or nut (the member) and the fixed stub, rod or neck it threads onto (the seat), in one object. The member starts resting loose on top of the stub, captive on the stub's axis: it cannot be picked up, carried or placed, so no pick acts on it. insert grips it in place and pushes it down the lead-in to the thread start (chamfer_mm + 3 mm down); twist clockwise seen from above runs it down the thread, engage_turns turns to seated, while the resisting torque rises from start_torque_nm to final_torque_nm. depth_mm counts down from the stub top; turns and angle_deg count clockwise from the start. Picking a loose member and starting it on a stub is not modelled.
templates.model: revolute joint coupled to a prismatic joint (helical equality) with a friction torque ramp
templates.caveat: Threads are an approximation: a helical joint with a torque ramp; no thread flanks, cross-threading or galling. A screen, not a promise.

params.name: diameter_mm
params.description: Outer diameter of the moving part

params.name: engage_turns
params.description: Turns from the thread start to seated

params.name: start_torque_nm
params.description: Running torque at the thread start

templates.description: A handwheel on a vertical stem with a resistive torque over its travel.
templates.note: A valve or any round handwheel on a vertical stem, the wheel 110 mm above the table. It starts closed at its stop and opens counter-clockwise seen from above (twist ccw); angle_deg counts counter-clockwise from closed. Closing a valve that starts closed is not modelled.
templates.model: revolute joint with a resistive torque curve and travel stops
templates.caveat: Valves are an approximation: a resistive torque curve on a revolute joint; no packing or seat dynamics.

params.name: spokes
params.description: Number of spokes (0: a solid disc)

templates.description: A fixed socket with a chamfer and a clearance, and a plug that starts free on the table.
templates.note: A connector and its port, a peg and its hole, a vial and its holder: one object holds both, the plug standing free on the table 40 mm beside its socket (do not add the plug as a separate part). depth_mm is the plug tip's depth below the socket mouth, seated at the socket's depth_mm.
templates.model: rigid socket and plug with contact, an insertion friction and an optional latch click

params.name: latch
params.description: A latch clicks when the plug is seated

templates.description: An open box: a fixed destination or a free body.
templates.note: A tote, tray, basket or box that picks drop into (fixed true unless it moves).
templates.model: static or free rigid box walls

params.name: fixed
params.description: Fixed to the table (otherwise a free body)

templates.description: A rigid part: a library or uploaded mesh (ref), or a box or cylinder of the given size.
templates.note: A rigid item: shape box or cylinder (cylinder: size_x_mm is the diameter, size_y_mm is ignored) with ref null; shape mesh only for an uploaded part, with ref upload:<id>.
templates.model: free rigid body (exact convex pieces, or CoACD hulls for scans and uploads)

params.name: shape
params.description: Mesh from ref, or a procedural box or cylinder

params.name: size_y_mm
params.description: Size along y (box; ignored for a cylinder)

params.name: mass_g
params.description: Mass (box and cylinder; a mesh uses its material)

templates.description: A large flat panel (a solar module) resting on two mounting rails against their end stops, with a threaded clamp on a post beside its edge.
templates.note: A solar module or any large flat panel on two mounting rails along local y, with a clamp (a 13 mm hex member on a post) at the middle of its -y long edge, 25 mm out. The panel starts resting on the rails, start_gap_mm short of their end stops at its +y edge; a pick (handle panel, target null) lifts it and sets it back on the rails, which stands for setting it down there (bringing it from a crate or stand is not modelled: list that in unsupported, nearest primitive suction), and gap_mm at_most says it sits against the stops. The clamp is a threaded member: insert it to its thread start (4 mm down), then twist cw; it seats after 3 turns of 1.25 mm pitch, its torque rising from 0.3 N m to clamp_torque_nm. clamp_torque_nm (the state) is how tight it got: judge the tightening by clamp_torque_nm at_least (at most the param), not by the wrist's torque_nm, which stays just under it. The panel's centre and the clamp lie (width_mm / 2 + 25) / 2 mm either side of the pose along local y.
templates.model: free rigid slab on two static rails with end stops; the clamp is a threaded member on a post (revolute and prismatic joints coupled by a helical tendon, with a friction torque ramp)
templates.caveat: The clamp is an approximation: a 13 mm hex modelled 15 mm tall so the simulated socket can seat (a standard M8 nut is 6.8 mm tall), on a helical joint with a torque ramp; it does not press the panel. The panel is a rigid slab.

params.name: width_mm
params.description: Panel width (along y, the way the rails run)

params.name: start_gap_mm
params.description: Gap between the panel's edge and the rail stops at the start

params.name: clamp_torque_nm
params.description: Torque that seats the clamp (its thread's final torque)

templates.description: A square floor tile laid on a fresh mortar bed, standing proud of its finished level until it is pressed in.
templates.note: A floor or wall tile on a fresh mortar or adhesive bed. The tile starts laid on the bed, proud_mm above its finished level. A pick (handle part, target null) lifts it and lays it back on the bed (laying it from a stack is not modelled: unsupported, nearest primitive suction). A push (handle part) presses it: the bed gives at bed_yield_n plus bed_hardening_n_mm for every mm it sinks (the tile's weight helps), keeps its set and lets the tile spring back up to 0.3 mm; it stops a tile 3 mm below its level. Judge the press by height_err_mm at_most (how far the top ends from its level, either way) and tilt_deg at_most.
templates.model: free rigid tile on a 3 x 3 grid of plastic bed cells (vertical slides that yield, harden and keep their set)
templates.caveat: The mortar bed is an approximation: nine plastic cells that yield and harden linearly and keep their set; no flow, suction or curing. A screen, not a promise.

params.name: proud_mm
params.description: How far the laid tile stands above its finished level

params.name: bed_yield_n
params.description: Total force at which the fresh bed starts to give

params.name: bed_hardening_n_mm
params.description: Extra force per mm the bed needs as it gives

templates.description: A round spring-return push button in a bezel, on a wall or on a desk console; a press past its actuation point latches the call.
templates.note: A call button, a push button or a switch. mount wall: a plate standing on the table, its face through the pose and facing local -y (yaw_deg turns it), the button's centre height_mm up; push it with approach front. mount desk: a console height_mm tall, the button on top facing up; push it with approach top. A press past 70 % of its travel latches pressed to 1; the button springs back when the tool lets go, so travel_mm reads 0 at the end: judge it by pressed at_least 1.
templates.model: prismatic joint with a preloaded return spring and an end stop, and a latch that records a press past the actuation point

params.name: mount
params.description: On a wall (it faces sideways) or a desk console (it faces up)

params.name: actuation_force_n
params.description: Force that presses it to its actuation point

params.name: proud_mm
params.description: How far the button stands out of its bezel at rest

params.name: height_mm
params.description: Wall: the button's centre above the table; desk: the console's height

templates.description: A machine enclosure whose door slides sideways: a front leaf and a roof leaf over the loading opening, moved by a fin handle on the roof.
templates.note: A machine with a guard door that slides sideways, loaded from above (a machine tool, a test chamber, an enclosure): the pose is the centre of its loading opening (width_mm along local y, the machine depth_mm along local x, its front facing local -x). The door starts closed over the opening and slides toward local -y to open (travel_mm 0 closed, positive open): hook_pull its handle (a fin on top, approach top) to open it, push it (handle door) to shut it. A fixture bin or a part inside the machine stands on the machine bed under the opening, inside its interior (see the layout rules).
templates.model: prismatic joint with friction loss and end stops (a drawer's slide, turned sideways)

params.name: width_mm
params.description: Loading opening width, along the slide

params.name: travel_mm
params.description: Door travel to the open stop

params.name: handle_mm
params.description: Height of the fin handle above the roof

handles.handle: the lip or handle at the free edge or front, or a sliding door's fin (hook it to pull open)
handles.head: the latch head, a slot or a wing (twist it)
handles.member: the cap, coupling, nut or clamp, captive on its stub or post (insert or twist it)
handles.seat: the fixed threaded seat (no primitive acts on it)
handles.plug: the free plug or connector (grasp, insert or push it)
handles.socket: the fixed socket (no primitive acts on it; the plug goes in)
handles.bin: the open box (a destination for picks)
handles.part: the part itself, or a tile on its bed (pick it, or press it)
handles.panel: the panel on its rails (a pick lifts it and sets it back)
